title: Quotient-Categorical Representations for Bellman-Compatible Average-Reward Distributional Reinforcement Learning
claim: Translating a distribution together with its support grid preserves its coefficients, but translating it against a fixed grid distorts them.
layout: 2 panels side by side, top-to-bottom within each, dashed alignment guides
description: Two panels with lollipop-style stem plots of a categorical distribution on five atoms, θ1 to θ5. Panel (a), "Law and grid shifted together", is in purple. The top row shows the original law η^{p,0}. Below it is the same law shifted by c, with its grid moved along with it. Dashed vertical guides and a double-headed arrow labelled c show the shift. The caption underneath reads "coefficients unchanged: p = (.08, .22, .38, .23, .09)". Panel (b), "Law shifted, grid fixed", has the same top row. Its bottom row switches to magenta. Hollow dashed purple stems mark the shifted atoms that fall between grid points. Arrows split the mass between neighbours, with labels ×.38 and ×.62. An arrow marked "clipped to θ5" shows the mass beyond the last atom being folded in. The caption reads "coefficients changed: q = (.03, .13, .28, .32, .23)". The eye goes first to the magenta bottom-right panel.
caption: (a) Shifting a law together with its grid leaves its coefficients $p$ unchanged (Lemma [ref]). (b) Shifting the law against a fixed grid moves its atoms off the grid. Projection then splits each atom between its two neighbors and clips mass beyond the last atom, giving $q\neq p$.
abstract: Average-reward reinforcement learning requires estimating the gain and a state-dependent bias, which solves the Poisson equation only up to an additive constant. Distributional analogues of the bias inherit this same ambiguity. We introduce a quotient-space formulation in which state-indexed laws are identified up to a common translation, together with a categorical parameterization that respects this symmetry. On this space, we define a projected average-reward distributional operator and show that it is well-defined, non-expansive in a coordinate CramÃ©r metric, and admits fixed points. We interpret the projected fixed points through geometrically-stopped differential returns, whose categorical operators are contractive and whose fixed points converge in the Abel sense to a canonical fixed point of the projected undiscounted operator. We show that the means of the projected fixed points match the scalar bias up to an error caused by endpoint clipping of the categorical projections, and we bound this error. Finally, we establish almost-sure convergence and finite-iteration residual bounds for temporal-difference recursions with gain-centered rewards under i.i.d. and Markovian sampling. When the gain is unknown, we couple the recursion with an online gain estimator and prove the same guarantees under Markovian sampling, with a bound on the gain error.
